physicalNotes: Radius 1.35 Jupiter radii from Lillo-Box et al. 2026 (2026arXiv260719756L), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026arXiv260719756L/abstract): 96,514.2 km at 71,492 km per Jupiter radius. GM from the mass 2.27 Jupiter masses (Lillo-Box et al. 2026, the mass the NASA Exoplanet Archive's composite table adopts (2026arXiv260719756L), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive, https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026arXiv260719756L/abstract) times JPL's Jupiter GM. A sphere: no oblateness is measured.

sources.period: Lillo-Box et al. 2026 (2026arXiv260719756L), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname LILLO_BOX_ET_AL_2026): P 3.1856381 d
sources.shape: Lillo-Box et al. 2026 (2026arXiv260719756L), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname LILLO_BOX_ET_AL_2026): a/R* 6.91; Lillo-Box et al. 2026 (2026arXiv260719756L), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname LILLO_BOX_ET_AL_2026): inclination 82.24 degrees
sources.eccentricity: No archive row states an eccentricity; the orbit is taken as circular
sources.phase: Lillo-Box et al. 2026 (2026arXiv260719756L), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname LILLO_BOX_ET_AL_2026): transit mid-time 2459850.81238 BJD, taken as BJD_TDB; with its period, the row that predicts 2026-01-01 best (1 sigma 1 min)
sources.orientation: Display convention: transit photometry does not measure the orbit's position angle on the sky, so the ascending node is set at position angle 0 (celestial north).
